new_statements.quote: [p. 77, §1.3.1 L'accent] Le bayot possède l’accent de mot qui est bien senti sur la dernière syllabe : il n’est pas distinctif (exemples 1 et 2). Il a une fonction démarcative. Il existe par ailleurs au niveau de la phrase un accent d’insistance (voir exemples 3 et 4, 5 et 6). Celui-ci a des effets d’allongement de la voyelle de la syllabe. [p. 78, §1.3.3 La question des tons] Nous n’avons pas relevé la présence de tonèmes [...]. [p. 229, conclusion] [la langue bayot] connaît le trait plus ATR, [...] posséde des voyelles nasales et des consonnes légèrement rétroflexes et n’est pas une langue à tons.
new_statements.translation: [p. 77] Bayot has word accent, which is clearly felt on the last syllable: it is not distinctive (examples 1 and 2). It has a demarcative function. In addition there is, at sentence level, an accent of insistence (examples 3-6), which lengthens the vowel of the syllable. [p. 78] We have not found tonemes [...]. [p. 229] [Bayot] has the +ATR feature, has nasal vowels and slightly retroflex consonants, and is not a tone language.
new_statements.citation: Diagne, Mbacké. 2009. Le bayot: langue atlantique nord, groupe bak, sous-groupe jóola. Thèse de doctorat, INALCO Paris, xii+302 pp. (= Diagne 2011a. Description du bayot, langue atlantique, groupe Bak, sous-groupe joola: phonologie, morphologie, syntaxe. Leipzig: Éditions universitaires européennes.)
new_statements.locator: Part 1 Phonologie, §1.3 Prosodie: §1.3.1 L'accent p. 77, §1.3.2 L'intonation p. 78, §1.3.3 La question des tons p. 78; conclusion p. 229; also §1.2.5.3 p. 76 and the glottal-stop paragraph p. 46 (file, PDF page = printed page)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened from the mirror. the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'INSTITUT NATIONAL DES LANGUES ET CIVILISATIONS ORIENTALES', Author 'Mbacké Diagne', 314 pp., Word 2013 export 2018-08-01. Title page (PDF p.1) reads exactly as the first reader says: 'THESE DE DOCTORAT UNIQUE.. Mbacké Diagne / Le Bayot / Langue Atlantique Nord, groupe bak, sous groupe jóola / Sous la direction de Stéphane Robert.. Soutenue le 27 mars 2009', jury Robert, Podzniakov, Creissels, Rougé, Voisin = the cited INALCO thesis (theses.fr 2009INAL0005): same work. Quotes checked against the text layer by form-feed page: p.77 §1.3.1 'L’accent : (')' -> 'Le bayot possède l’accent de mot qui est bien senti sur la dernière sylla…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (bayo1255 has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project; this is the first placement statement: final, non-contrastive, demarcative word accent; no tone)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the last syllable of the word; it is non-contrastive (non-distinctive) and demarcative. Separately, a phrase-level emphatic accent ('accent d'insistance') lengthens the vowel of the syllable it falls on (e.g. 'boo 'jusqu'à' vs bo 'à'). No tonemes were found; the language is stated not to be a tone language. Intonation: assertions fall more sharply from the antepenultimate syllable; questions, injunctions and interjections rise.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for the word accent. Related remarks: §1.3.2 (p. 78) marks an accent (') on the antepenultimate syllable of an assertive utterance (áñí ma'le evÜ 'l'enfant pleure') in connection with the falling intonation slope; §1.2.5.3 (p. 76) says that in word-internal sequences of different vowels the last vowel loses intensity and length, whereas across a word boundary vowels keep their intensity (') or length (ex. Ka'taaku 'crâne', o'doÏ 'fourmilière'); p. 46 treats the glottal stop as non-phonemic, 'un relâchement des cordes vocales dû à la présence de l'accent sur la dernière syllabe ouverte d'un mot bisyllabique'.
new_statements.identity_note: Diagne's thesis describes Bayot as spoken around Nyassia (arrondissement de Nyassia, Ziguinchor, Casamance) and bases the phonology explicitly on the kugere dialect (Etomé, Kailou, Kassoulou, Kadiéné, Darsalam; p. 19 'Pour faire l'étude phonologique du kugere'), recognising a second dialect kuhiŋe/ehi/essin (Bafikan, Dialan, Diohère, Kureng, Etafune); Glottolog bayo1255 'Kugere-Kuxinge' covers exactly these two. The Guinea-Bissau variety edámme/erámme/kusikuaay mentioned in the dictionary introduction is Glottolog Arame-Gubaare, a separate languoid, and is not the basis of either description.
